note: Controlled benchmark of the v0.5.1 engine (drawn domain scenes for non-software heroes, bigger headline tiers, dark featured pricing tier). Haiku 5.5 without vs with the MCP, identical SPEC.md, same 60-call budget, four never-seen domains (ashby coffee roastery, cornerstone conveyancing law firm, oakhaven pottery studio, cadence restaurant-scheduling software), engine frozen for the run. RESULT: WORSE than v0.5.0 (engine 0/8; product-visual 5.25 vs 8.13). DIAGNOSIS from the judges' own words: the generic library scenes read as generic or wrong (a courthouse for conveyancing where the baseline showed a specific client-portal UI; a LOOM for a pottery studio because the keyword router matched 'craft'; a generic cafe where the baseline drew a labelled coffee bag with a cupping panel) and the engine's feature illustrations (one icon on an abstract motif) were weaker than the baselines' bespoke per-feature drawings. The scene override also replaced product mockups that were the better hero. CONFOUNDS: the Ashby MCP agent's first build accidentally used a brief another agent had overwritten in the shared scratchpad (it noticed and rebuilt); the Cadence MCP agent had to force heroStyle:'product' (the software check was too fragile, fixed afterwards) and hand-edited the footer tagline and touch-target sizes; the Ashby MCP agent hand-edited the billing-button height. Next version (v0.6.0): let the model draw bespoke SVG for the hero and each feature, give it an illustration kit to compose from, and never override a supplied product mockup.
